half_step.text: The smallest distance in Western music: one fret on the guitar, one key to the next on a piano.

interval.text: The distance between two notes, counted in half steps and named by size (3rd, 5th…) and quality (major, minor, perfect).

octave.text: The same note 12 half steps higher or lower: it sounds like the same note, brighter or darker.

enharmonic.text: Two names for the same pitch, like C♯ and D♭. The key decides which name is correct.

root.text: The note a chord or scale is built on and named after: C is the root of C major and of Cmaj7.

degree.text: A note's place in the key, counted from the root: 1, 2, 3… A ♭ or ♯ means a half step lower or higher than in the major scale.

scale.text: A set of notes in order, defined by its pattern of steps from the root.

major_scale.text: The scale with the steps W W H W W W H. Most of harmony is explained from it.

relative_minor.text: The minor key with the same notes as a major key, built on its 6th degree (A minor for C major).

pentatonic.text: A five-note scale. The minor pentatonic is 1 ♭3 4 5 ♭7; the major pentatonic is 1 2 3 5 6.

mode.text: The notes of a scale played with a different note as home. Each mode has its own color.

tab.text: Guitar notation with six lines for the strings (high E on top) and numbers for the frets.

chord_tone.text: A note that belongs to the chord (root, 3rd, 5th, 7th…), as opposed to a passing note.

inversion.text: A chord with a note other than the root in the bass. C/E is C major in 1st inversion.

slash_chord.text: A chord written with the bass note after a slash: C/G means C with G in the bass.

seventh_chord.text: A triad plus a 7th: maj7, 7, m7, m7♭5, dim7…

dominant.text: The V chord of a key, or any 7 chord (1 3 5 ♭7). Its tension wants to resolve.

extension.text: Notes stacked above the 7th: 9, 11, 13 (and their altered forms ♭9, ♯9, ♯11, ♭13).

diatonic.text: Made only of the notes of the key. The diatonic chords of C are C Dm Em F G Am B°.

roman_numeral.text: Chords named by their degree in the key (I, ii, V7…), so a progression reads the same in any key.

voicing.text: Which notes of a chord you play, in what order and on which strings.

drop2.text: A four-note voicing made by moving the second note from the top of a close chord down an octave.

guide_tones.text: The 3rd and 7th of a chord: they tell the chord type and move smoothly from chord to chord.

voice_leading.text: Moving each note of a chord to the nearest note of the next one.

ii_v_i.text: The minor 7 on degree 2, the dominant on 5, and the major chord on 1: the most common progression in jazz.

turnaround.text: A short progression at the end of a form that leads back to the start.

tritone.text: The interval of three whole steps (6 frets). It splits the octave in half.

swing.text: Playing pairs of eighth notes long–short: the second one of each pair lands late.

comping.text: Accompanying with chords in rhythm behind a melody or a solo.

approach_note.text: A note a step away that leads into a target note.

enclosure.text: Surrounding a target note: the note above, the note below, then the target.

bpm.text: Beats per minute: how fast the music goes.
